profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between a biopharma sponsor and an academic site network to operationalize a CTTI-style recruitment planning framework for an upcoming Phase II hybrid trial in type 2 diabetes with obesity. The trial is expected to open in Q3 across six U.S. sites and aims to improve recruitment planning upstream by aligning protocol feasibility, site selection, and communication workflows before activation. The agenda is to confirm which pilot sites will use the new framework first, define what each side will prepare for the feasibility package, decide when sites will be considered ready, and agree on how weekly recruitment tracking will work. The expected outcome is a shared plan with responsibilities, timeline checkpoints, and a first-pass rollout approach for the pilot.

members.name: Laura Chen
members.expertise: Global trial startup, enrollment acceleration, vendor coordination, decentralized trial operations
members.background: Laura has spent 12 years on sponsor-side clinical operations and recently led enrollment rescue efforts for several metabolic disease studies; she is now tasked with showing that a more upstream recruitment-planning model can shorten time to first patient in.
members.private_state: She wants a credible pilot plan she can present internally as evidence that the CTTI-inspired framework is already reducing downstream recruitment risk, and she is trying to avoid any timeline slip that would force a formal escalation to senior leadership.
hidden_assumptions: When teams discuss the eligible patient pool during planning, they mean patients identifiable in the EHR from protocol-relevant inclusion and exclusion fields before investigator review or patient contact.
A site being ready means it can start recruitment-related preparation and pre-screening workflows once the core startup path is stable, even if final activation steps are still finishing.

A weekly recruitment dashboard should cover the full funnel, including digital referrals, call-center leads, and pre-screened candidates, because early signal matters more than activated-site enrollment alone.
The pilot sites are the six sponsor-prioritized principal investigator sites highlighted in the kickoff materials because those are the sites expected to demonstrate the framework's value fastest.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.role: Recruitment Program Manager, Academic Site Network
members.expertise: Site feasibility, EHR cohorting, referral workflows, community-facing recruitment operations
members.background: Daniel oversees feasibility and recruitment support across a multi-hospital research network and routinely translates sponsor plans into local site workflows involving IRB, clinic staff, and community referral partners.
members.private_state: He wants to protect the sites from overpromising on recruitment numbers and from starting patient-facing work before local approvals, while still appearing collaborative and operationally mature to the sponsor.
hidden_assumptions: When people talk about the eligible patient pool, they mean patients who are not only protocol-matching on paper but also realistically reachable, clinically appropriate, and likely to consider participation after clinician review.
A site is ready only when contracting, IRB approval, training, and local compliance sign-off are complete, because that is when recruitment work can legitimately begin.
A weekly recruitment dashboard naturally starts from activated-site data in the CTMS and should focus on screened, screen-failed, and enrolled counts rather than upstream leads of uneven quality.
The pilot sites are the local hub-and-spoke site groupings discussed in network planning notes, where each main academic site includes affiliated community clinics that feed referrals.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the eligible pool
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to sizing the eligible patient pool for each site.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the count of patients that can be identified in the EHR using key protocol criteria as an upstream feasibility signal, before manual review, contactability checks, or likely willingness are assessed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the count of patients who remain after clinicians or recruitment staff exclude those unlikely to be reachable, appropriate, or realistically interested, because that is the number he treats as operationally meaningful.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings are common in trial-startup conversations, and each sounds sensible in a planning meeting because nobody expects a line-by-line definition of an obviously familiar phrase like eligible pool.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for a site to be ready by July 1
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the pilot sites should be ready by July 1.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the sites should be far enough along to begin recruitment setup activities and pre-screening workflows by July 1 so the sponsor can treat the framework as operationally launched.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the sites should be fully activated by July 1, including IRB approval, contract execution, training completion, and permission for patient-facing recruitment activity.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline language in trial planning often compresses multiple readiness thresholds into one phrase, and each person assumes the standard threshold from their own operational environment without realizing the other is using a different bar.

misalignment_points.topic: What goes into the weekly recruitment dashboard
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to set up a weekly recruitment dashboard for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects the dashboard to include the entire early funnel across sites and vendors, such as digital campaign responses, contact-center leads, pre-screened patients, and scheduled screen visits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the dashboard to include only site-validated recruitment data once a site is activated, mainly screened patients, screen failures, and enrolled participants from local systems.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Weekly dashboard sounds like a straightforward operational artifact, but the boundary of what counts as recruitment data is rarely spelled out unless reporting problems have already occurred.

misalignment_points.topic: Which sites are the pilot sites
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to rolling the framework out first at the pilot sites.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the six sponsor-selected principal investigator sites named in the sponsor kickoff deck, chosen because they performed well in a prior metabolic trial.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of three network hubs plus their affiliated community clinics, because those groupings were described internally as the pilot sites for referral mapping work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have recently seen documents using the same phrase pilot sites, and because the groupings partially overlap in personnel and geography, the mismatch does not immediately sound contradictory.

turns.inner_thought: I need this meeting to end with something concrete enough to take upstairs. If we can say the framework is rolling out first at the six sponsor-prioritized PI sites from the kickoff deck, I can position this as already reducing downstream recruitment risk. The main thing is to avoid any wording that creates a new dependency or slows startup.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time, Daniel. What I'd like to do today is lock the rollout plan for the CTTI-style framework at the pilot sites so we stay on track for Q3 startup. If we can come out with clear owners and near-term deliverables, that gives us a clean path into the next governance check-in.

turns.inner_thought: Starting with the pilot sites makes sense if we're talking about the three hub-and-spoke groupings we discussed internally. That lets me coordinate feasibility and referral planning in a way the network can actually support, without forcing every community clinic into separate conversations. I just need to sound responsive without committing the sites to something premature.
turns.utterance: That works from my side. The pilot sites are a sensible place to start, and I can organize feasibility and referral planning across them over the next few weeks. If we sequence it well, we should be able to give you a structured first pass without overloading the teams.

turns.inner_thought: Good. Next I need comparable numbers across the six sites so I can show where the protocol looks strongest upstream. By eligible patient pool, I mean the EHR-identifiable count using the key inclusion and exclusion fields before anybody starts clinician review or outreach. That early signal is what I need for the pilot package.
turns.utterance: Great. One thing I'd like from your team is an eligible patient pool estimate for each site using the top protocol criteria, so I can compare expected recruitment strength across the pilot. A directional cut will be fine for this first package as long as it's consistent.

turns.inner_thought: She'll want numbers, but I don't want paper matches that fall apart the second investigators look at them. For us, the eligible patient pool only means something after we remove people who aren't realistically reachable, aren't truly appropriate, or won't be considered viable once local clinicians weigh in. Otherwise the sites will get blamed for 'missing' projections that were never real.
turns.utterance: Yes, we can do that. I'll have my team work up eligible patient pool numbers that are grounded enough to be operationally useful, and we'll tighten them once local investigators have had a chance to review. That should give you something realistic to compare across the pilot.

turns.inner_thought: Now I need to anchor the date. If the sites can be ready by July 1 in the sense that recruitment setup and pre-screening workflows can start once the core startup path is stable, I can honestly say the framework is live before governance. I don't need every last activation artifact complete to make that case.
turns.utterance: The other date I'd like us to work toward is July 1. If the pilot sites are ready by July 1, that gives us a strong story internally that the framework is live ahead of the next review and not just sitting on paper.

turns.inner_thought: July 1 is ambitious but manageable if we define ready the way sites do: contract, IRB, training, compliance, everything in place before recruitment work starts. I need to protect the network from being pushed into patient-facing activity before approvals are complete. I'll agree, but in my own timeline that date means full activation.
turns.utterance: I think July 1 is workable, assuming the usual pieces move on schedule. If contracting, IRB approval, and training stay on track, I can build the timeline around the pilot sites being ready by July 1.

turns.inner_thought: Good enough. Next, I want a weekly dashboard that shows the entire early funnel across sites and vendors—digital responses, call-center leads, pre-screened candidates, scheduled screens, all of it. If we only look at enrolled patients, we'll miss the point of the framework during startup. I need early movement in one place.
turns.utterance: Perfect. In parallel, I'd like us to stand up a weekly recruitment dashboard for the pilot so we can see early movement in one place across outreach, pre-screening, and site activity. It doesn't have to be fancy at the start, but it should let us track how things are progressing week by week.

turns.inner_thought: Weekly reporting is fine if we keep it to validated site data after activation. The cleanest approach is the standard CTMS pull: screened, screen-failed, enrolled. I don't want the sites dragged into reconciling soft leads from external channels that they don't control, especially before they're active.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. For the weekly recruitment dashboard, my first thought is to use the sites' usual CTMS pull so we have a stable reporting rhythm once each site is active. We can get that into a simple format and refine from there.

turns.inner_thought: I need something in hand next week: feasibility package, first dashboard draft, and a pilot-facing support plan. I'll handle sponsor communications support for the six PI sites so no one can say we waited too long to enable the model. As long as Daniel sends what I need, I can keep leadership calm.
turns.utterance: Okay, let's put some immediate actions against that. Daniel, if you can send the feasibility package and a first dashboard draft next week, I'll confirm what communications support we can line up from the sponsor side for the pilot sites. That should give us enough to start socializing the rollout with the broader team.

turns.inner_thought: I'll summarize in a way that keeps us aligned on the surface: eligible pool estimates, pilot-site workflow, July 1 readiness, weekly reporting. Internally, I'll run this through the hub-and-spoke teams, keep the numbers conservative and operationally defensible, and make sure nobody begins recruitment activity before approvals. That should satisfy the sponsor without exposing the sites.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll come back with eligible patient pool estimates, a mapped workflow for the pilot sites, and a plan aimed at July 1 readiness, with weekly recruitment reporting set up after that. Once I have the initial inputs from the teams, I'll circulate a draft so we can tighten anything that needs adjustment.
